title: The Transformer Block, Layer by Layer
summary: A transformer is one block repeated L times: attention to mix information between tokens, a feed-forward network to process each token, normalisation to keep numbers stable, and a residual stream that ties it all together. This lesson builds the block piece by piece and then counts every parameter to reproduce real model sizes.
objectives: Trace a token's vector through the residual stream of a pre-norm transformer block
Compute LayerNorm and RMSNorm by hand and explain why blocks normalise their inputs
Explain the feed-forward network, its 4× expansion and the SwiGLU variant
Explain why attention needs position information and how learned, sinusoidal and rotary encodings provide it
Count a transformer's parameters with 12·L·d² + V·d and reproduce GPT-2 small (124M) and Llama-2-7B (6.74B)
prerequisites: You should know scaled dot-product and multi-head attention from [Attention](/learn/model-foundations/attention), what an embedding table is from [Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings), and how a layer's parameters are counted from [A model is a function with knobs](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn).
